newsitem.title: USA: BEFORE THE BELL - Shiva, Loewen fall. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: BEFORE THE BELL - Shiva, Loewen fall. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]

text.p: The floor collapsed beneath Shiva Corp shares early Wednesday as investors fretted over the company's admission that fourth quarter earnings will be sharply below Wall Street expectations.
Before the market open, Shiva tumbled to trade in the 18-1/8 to 18-1/2 range, down from last night's 34-7/8 Nasdaq close.

Minutes after Tuesday's (corrects from "Monday's") market close, Shiva said it expects fourth quarter earnings of $0.05 to $0.07 per share, a small fraction of the First Call analysts' consensus view of $0.21 per share.

In the statement, Shiva said it expected total revenue for the quarter ended December 28, 1996 to be about $48 to $50 million, a decline from the $57.1 million reported in the third quarter ended in September.
The company reported $35.6 in revenues for the fourth quarter ended December 30, 1995.
Elsewhere, Loewen Group Inc's NYSE-listed shares fell to 35 from 40-7/8 after Service Corp International withdrew its four-month hostile takeover bid.
Service Corp shares rose to 29-3/4 from 27-5/8 in response to the news, traders said.
In Focus Systems rose 2-3/4 to 25-1/2 after announcing this morning fourth quarter results will be above Wall Street's $0.36 per share consensus estimate.
Intel Corp added 5/8 to 144 on continued optimism about the company's latest generation computer microprocessor, the MMX, unveiled today.
Motorola Inc shares climbed to 62-1/2 from 61-3/4 after Morgan Stanley upgraded the stock to outperform from neutral.
